# s253 — check must not report a collision when a branch retitles an existing item

`slicer check` warns when a sibling worktree has an id under a different title (s185, `_sibling_collisions` in `src/slicer/check.py`). Retitling an existing item on a slice branch trips the same warning, and its advice, to file this checkout's item under a new id, would duplicate the item. A collision is two different filings of one id, so only an id that is new on both sides can collide.

**Findings:** s251 relay, 2026-10-11: retitling s251 on its branch warned 'will collide on merge' and advised refiling under a new id · **Size:** S · **Trees:** src/slicer, tests, docs

**2026-10-11** — Ready for review: check's sibling collision warning now fires only for ids absent from the merge base of this checkout and the sibling, so retitling an existing item on a branch no longer warns. The git allowlist gains one read-only form, merge-base COMMIT COMMIT (full object names only). Falls back to warning when there is no merge base or no readable index at the base. 6 new tests plus 2 allowlist refusals, mutation-checked; full suite 1643 OK; relay gate VERDICT: PASS (Sonnet high implementer).

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** other sibling-worktree reports (in-work, review, sibling-only items); changing merge-index; renumbering ids.

## Why

On 2026-10-11, during the s251 relay, s251 was retitled on its slice branch after its scope changed. `slicer check` then warned "s251 is '...' here but '...' in worktree slicer; the two will collide on merge. File this checkout's item under a new id before merging." It is the same item, and only one side changed the title, so `merge-index` takes the change cleanly. A false warning that recommends a harmful fix trains people to ignore the real one.

Decision (owner, 2026-10-11): (a). Read the merge base's index (`git merge-base` of the two checkouts, then `git show BASE:./.slicer/index.json`) and warn only for ids absent from the base. Alternatives (b) compare the filing `key` and (c) soften the message were rejected: (b) does not fix the common case because most items have no key, and (c) still advises refiling a legitimate retitle. This needs `merge-base COMMIT COMMIT` in the `vcs.py` allowlist. With no merge base or no readable base index, the check keeps today's warning.
